options.text: Very different size and gravity could change the atmosphere the planet can hold and make conditions unsafe for life as we know it.
Only sunlight matters, so size and gravity can change freely without affecting habitability.
A much larger planet would always be colder, because size alone sets temperature.
Stronger gravity would only swap day and night and leave habitability unchanged.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Avni asks whether Earth could stay habitable if the planet were much smaller with much weaker gravity, or much larger with much stronger gravity.

part_answers.answer: Planet size links to gravity strength, which affects atmosphere retention and living conditions, not only sunlight or day–night order.

teacher.key_rationale: Habitability depends on more than sunlight; size and gravity shape atmosphere and living conditions. Ignoring gravity, equating size with temperature alone, or tying gravity only to day–night all miss that hinge.
